sources.claim: GNU Time v1.9 obtains the child rusage through wait3 and stores it in the report structure.
%M prints ru_maxrss through the configured KiB accessor and does not read procfs.
Linux is configured as returning ru_maxrss in KiB; the rusage-kb accessor is therefore a no-op conversion.
The Linux ru_maxrss unit assumption and the direct maxrss accessor are explicit.
GNU Time v1.9 creates the measured command with ordinary fork and then execvp.
glibc implements wait3 by calling wait4 with WAIT_ANY.
The Linux glibc wait4 implementation passes the rusage pointer to the wait4 system call when the ABI is available.
Linux posix_spawn uses clone with CLONE_VM and CLONE_VFORK, so the child shares the caller's memory space until execve or _exit and the caller is suspended.
Linux exec_mmap records the old address space's RSS high-water in signal->maxrss before releasing the old mm.
An ordinary non-thread fork creates a fresh zeroed signal structure before copying the child's memory state.
A fork without CLONE_VM duplicates the mm and resets the child mm high-water RSS to its current approximate RSS.
Linux getrusage uses the signal high-water fields, obtains live mm high-water through setmax_mm_hiwater_rss, and converts pages to KiB.
Linux records group maxrss at exit and returns child rusage from wait4 using RUSAGE_BOTH.
get_mm_rss uses the approximate per-cpu-counter read, while get_mm_rss_sum and setmax_mm_hiwater_rss expose the distinct paths.
proc status sums RSS components and takes the maximum of cached high-water and current RSS; smaps uses a page-table walk.
Per-cpu updates are batched, the sum path folds every online/dying CPU local value, and the default batch is max(32, nr_online_cpus()*2).
The read accessor returns the shared count while the sum accessor invokes the full per-cpu sum.
RUSAGE_BOTH is the internal rusage selector used by sys_wait4.
Linux documents ru_maxrss in KiB and distinguishes child accounting from a process-tree maximum.
wait3 is a library function implemented on Linux over wait4 and returns child rusage.
The proc documentation distinguishes scalable RSS counters from smaps page-table scanning.

verified: The installed GNU Time binary enters through wait3 and formats %M from wait-provided ru_maxrss.
The installed package is configured for Linux ru_maxrss KiB semantics according to the matching upstream v1.9 source.
The host kernel headers use approximate per-cpu reads for get_mm_rss and summed per-cpu reads for proc memory reporting.
The upstream v7.0 per-cpu counter batch is max(32, online CPUs * 2), which is 64 pages for this 32-CPU host.
All 136 direct rows have parent wait4 ru_maxrss equal to the largest probe self ru_maxrss sample; this verifies direct-path agreement but not launcher independence.
The capture records os.posix_spawn taskset exec, and upstream glibc/Linux sources document the CLONE_VM/CLONE_VFORK, exec_mmap, ordinary fork, and dup_mm paths used to interpret that topology.
inference: Unflushed RSS per-cpu residues are a plausible explanation for the 0788 GNU-time-to-proc gaps; the 0789 known-page and affinity controls must test it.

The direct taskset exec can retain the capture process's prior mm high-water in the probe signal maxrss, while GNU Time's ordinary fork resets that inherited signal state; the direct 17--19 MiB startup samples versus roughly 1.8 MiB proc RSS match this source-backed interpretation.

Direct wait4 and GNU-time %M must not be pooled as interchangeable observations in this packet because their launcher topologies differ; use an ordinary fork/exec or fresh low-high-water helper for the decisive same-topology comparison.
The exact Ubuntu AWS kernel and glibc vendor C-source correspondence was not independently diffed, so upstream source behavior is not asserted as a complete vendor-source proof.
